item.title: Elder Eraka: “O Eraka, painful are sensual pleasures! O Eraka, not happiness are sensual pleasures! One who desires sensual pleasures, desires suffering. One who does…
item.description:
Elder Eraka:
“O Eraka, painful are sensual pleasures!
O Eraka, not happiness are sensual pleasures!
One who desires sensual pleasures, desires suffering.
One who does not desire sensual pleasures, does not desire suffering.
O Eraka, know this as it is.”

From: Theragāthā 1.93

item.title: “Householder, having known that sensual desire is a defilement of the mind, that noble disciple abandons sensual desire, the defilement of the mind; having known…
item.description:
“Householder, having known that sensual desire is a defilement of the mind, that noble disciple abandons sensual desire, the defilement of the mind; having known that ill-will is a defilement of the mind, he abandons ill-will; having known that sloth and torpor are defilements of the mind, he abandons sloth and torpor; having known that restlessness and remorse are defilements of the mind, he abandons restlessness and remorse; having known that doubt is a defilement of the mind, he abandons doubt. This, householder, is called a noble disciple of great wisdom, of broad wisdom, who has entered the sphere of clear vision, endowed with wisdom. This is called being endowed with wisdom.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.61
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Elder Nun Selā: You will not escape, You will not escape this world. What use is this practice of seclusion to you? Enjoy sensual pleasures…
item.description:
Elder Nun Selā:

You will not escape,
You will not escape this world.
What use is this practice of seclusion to you?
Enjoy sensual pleasures —
Do not have regrets later.

Sensual pleasures are like swords and spears —
They cut the aggregates to pieces.
What you call the pleasure of life —
For me, that sensual pleasure
Is no longer enticing.

Everywhere, delight is destroyed.
The mass of darkness,
The blinding darkness, has been shattered.
Know this, O Evil One —
You are Māra,
You are defeated.

From: Therīgāthā 3.7
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: - “Venerable sir, do you know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings?” - “Friend, I know the release, the escape, the seclusion for…
item.description:
- “Venerable sir, do you know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings?”
- “Friend, I know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings.”
- “But how, venerable sir, do you know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings?”
The destruction of delight in renewed existence,
The cessation of perception and consciousness,
The stilling of feelings —
Thus, friend, I know the release,
The escape and seclusion
For all kinds of beings.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.2
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye—these are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing.…
item.description:
“Monks, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye—these are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. Sounds cognizable by the ear … Odors cognizable by the nose … Tastes cognizable by the tongue … Tangibles cognizable by the body—these are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. These, monks, are the five strands of sensual pleasure.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 26 – Ariyapariyesanāsutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, before my enlightenment, while I was still a bodhisatta, not yet fully enlightened, I thought: ‘What is the gratification, what is the peril, what…
item.description:
“Monks, before my enlightenment, while I was still a bodhisatta, not yet fully enlightened, I thought: ‘What is the gratification, what is the peril, what is the escape in the case of form? … in the case of feeling? … perception? … formations? … consciousness?’ Then, monks, I thought: ‘The pleasure and joy that arise dependent on form — that is the gratification of form. That form is impermanent, suffering, subject to change — that is the peril of form. The removal and abandonment of desire and lust for form — that is the escape from form.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.26
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Like a pit of filth Accumulated for many years — So too, a defiled person Is very hard to cleanse. Monks, know such a person…
item.description:
“Like a pit of filth
Accumulated for many years —
So too, a defiled person
Is very hard to cleanse.

Monks, know such a person —
Attached to households,
With evil desires, evil intentions,
Evil conduct, evil practices.

All of you, being of one mind,
Should shun such a person.
Blow him away like dust,
Throw him out like rubbish.

Expel the verbose one,
The fake ascetic.
Having expelled evil desires,
Evil conduct, evil practices —

Keep yourselves pure,
Live with the pure,
Mindful, dwelling together,
Wise, and make an end of suffering.”

From: Sutta Nipāta 2.6
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, if there were no gratification in the world, beings would not become lustful for the world. But because there is gratification in the world,…
item.description:
“Monks, if there were no gratification in the world, beings would not become lustful for the world. But because there is gratification in the world, beings become lustful for the world. If there were no peril in the world, beings would not become disenchanted with the world. But because there is peril in the world, beings become disenchanted with the world. If there were no escape from the world, beings would not escape from the world. But because there is escape from the world, beings escape from the world.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.105
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Elder Nun Sundarī Nandā: Nandā, look at this body — Diseased, impure, stinking. Develop the mind on foulness, One-pointed, well-concentrated. As this body, so that…
item.description:
Elder Nun Sundarī Nandā:

Nandā, look at this body —
Diseased, impure, stinking.
Develop the mind on foulness,
One-pointed, well-concentrated.

As this body, so that body —
As that body, so this body —
Foul, rotting —
Only fools delight in it.

Thus contemplate this body,
Day and night without fatigue.
With your own wisdom,
Therefore escape.
With your own wisdom,
Escape pride in beauty,
And see truly
What fools see.

This city is built of bones,
Plastered with flesh and blood.
Within dwell aging and death,
Conceit and hypocrisy.

Without heedlessness,
Rightly contemplate that body —
The true nature of this body
Is seen inside and out.
I am disenchanted with the body,
My mind is dispassionate.
Without heedlessness, free from bonds,
I am at peace, stilled.

From: Therīgāthā 5.4
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “If anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the unwholesome,’ monks, he would speak rightly of the five hindrances. Indeed, the entire heap of the unwholesome,…
item.description:
“If anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the unwholesome,’ monks, he would speak rightly of the five hindrances. Indeed, the entire heap of the unwholesome, monks, is just the five hindrances. What five? The hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrance of ill-will, the hindrance of sloth and torpor, the hindrance of restlessness and remorse, the hindrance of doubt. If anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the unwholesome,’ he would speak rightly of the five hindrances. Indeed, the entire heap of the unwholesome is just the five hindrances.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.52
📖 Read this sutta
